verses.1: Having heard that divine-like and amazing story, Lakshmana was greatly pleased and spoke these words to Rama.
verses.2: Lakshmana asked Rama how those two, the Brahmin and the king, who had abandoned their bodies and were respected by the gods, managed to regain a physical form.
verses.3: Having heard Lakshmana's words, Rama, whose valor is truth, then narrated the story of the great-souled Vasishtha.
verses.4: O best of Raghu's lineage, in that pot, which was filled with the radiant semen of the two great souls (Mitra and Varuna), two radiant Brahmins, who were excellent sages, were born.
verses.5: First, the divine sage Agastya was born there, and having said "I am not your son," Mitra then departed from him.
verses.6: That semen of Mitra, which had previously been placed in Urvashi, was born in that pot where the semen of Varuna was also present.
verses.7: Then, after some time, Vasishtha, born of Mitra and Varuna and endowed with radiance, was born as the priest of Ikshvaku.
verses.8: O gentle one, the exceedingly radiant Ikshvaku chose that blameless Vasishtha, as soon as he was born, to be the family priest for the prosperity of our lineage.
verses.9: O gentle one, thus has been narrated the birth of the great-souled Vasistha, who had an unprecedented body; now listen to how it happened with Nimi.
verses.10: All those wise sages, having seen the king Nimi bodiless, then engaged him in the initiation rites for the sacrifice.
verses.11: And the best among the twice-born, accompanied by citizens and servants, protected that body of the king with fragrances, garlands, and clothes.
verses.12: Then, when the sacrifice was concluded, Bhrigu said: O king, I am pleased with you, and I shall restore your consciousness.
verses.13: And all the gods, being very pleased, thus spoke to Nimi's spirit: "O royal sage, choose a boon; where should your mind be fixed?"
verses.14: Thus spoken to by all the gods, Nimi's spirit then said: "O best among gods, may I dwell in the eyes of all beings."
verses.15: The gods then spoke to Nimi's spirit, saying, "Indeed, you will move as air within the eyes of all beings."
verses.16: O King, for your sake, the eyes will blink repeatedly for rest, as you move within them as air.
verses.17: Having spoken thus, all the gods departed to their respective abodes, and the great-souled sages then collected Nimi's body.
verses.18: Then, the great-souled sages, for the sake of a son for Nimi, placed the fire-stick there and performed churning with might and mantra-oblations.
verses.19: From the churned fire-stick, a great ascetic appeared, who was called Mithi because of the churning, became Janaka due to his birth, and was known as Vaideha because he was born from the bodyless Nimi.
verses.20: Thus, the ancestor of Janaka, the king of Videha, was the greatly effulgent Mithi, from whom this region became known as Maithila. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे सप्तपञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 57 ।। Thus ends the fifty-seventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
